text.headline: US Stocks under pressure in stocks
text.tone: Rising volatility weighed on US stocks, though one day's trading is not enough to establish the cause.
lead: US large caps (EB US 100) fell 4.6%, the most significant move of the session on the [[markets|Financial Markets]]. In contrast, VIX volatility index rose 15.8%, a sign that investors did not move in a single direction. Copper moved the same way, which gives the move more weight.
A likely reading: investors moved from shares towards gold, a classic search for safety. The yen firmed as shares fell, a typical move when investors cut risk.
Across asset classes, EUR/USD fell 0.02% and Bitcoin rose 2.0%. Expected volatility (the VIX) rose as shares fell: investors paid more for protection.

What to watch: whether the main move holds over the next sessions or fades, and whether other markets begin to follow. A broader shift would confirm today's reading; a quick reversal would point to a short-lived adjustment. The [[outlook|Market Outlook]] places it in the longer trend.

briefs.markets: US 10-year yield fell 3 bp to 5.04% (latest data: Nov 19), leaving the gap over the 2-year at +28 bp. The [[markets|Financial Markets]] page has yields, commodities and currencies.
briefs.energy: Brent crude rose 0.04% to $92.94 (latest data: Nov 17); US natural gas (Henry Hub) fell 3.1% to $3.10 (latest data: Nov 17). Benchmarks, power prices and supply data on the [[energy|Energy Terminal]].
briefs.crypto: Bitcoin rose 2.0% to $61,314; EUR/USD fell 0.02% to 1.0990. Live rates and a converter on [[crypto|Crypto & Currencies]].
briefs.metals: Gold rose 2.9% to $3,619; Copper fell 2.7% to $12,230/t. Precious and base metals on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]].
briefs.estate: House prices are rising in 61 of the 69 countries we track over the past year; Moldova leads at +33.7%. Country data on the [[estate|Estate Index]].
briefs.corporate: This week's top-ranked bank is East West Bank and the top company is APA Corporation, under a risk-on backdrop. Rankings on the [[corporate|Corporate Monitor]].
briefs.outlook: Our quarterly outlook reads the backdrop as risk-off; Cybersecurity leads the five themes we follow. Full rankings on the [[outlook|Market Outlook]].
briefs.islamic: EB Shariah US 100 fell 4.8% to 105.21; it is +2.7% this year against +1.0% for the unscreened market. Screens and funds on [[islamic|Islamic Investment]].
